security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly false positives from safe examples, markdown paths, GitHub Actions syntax, and loop variables. The only confirmed risk is the automated update shell example, which can alter dependency state if executed without explicit approval and testing.

remediation.issue: Automated update script can modify dependency files and installed packages.
remediation.suggestion: Keep auto-fix and upgrade commands opt-in, require explicit user approval, and recommend tests plus rollback steps before execution.

remediation.issue: Scanner examples may contact package registries and vulnerability services.
remediation.suggestion: Document expected network behavior and allow users to choose offline or organization-approved scanners when needed.

content.value_statement: Dependency risk grows across package ecosystems and CI pipelines. This skill guides vulnerability scanning, SBOM creation, prioritization, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Detects common npm, Python, Go, and Rust dependency manifests.
Shows scanner patterns for npm audit, Safety, govulncheck, and cargo audit.
Prioritizes vulnerabilities by severity, exploitability, and fix availability.
Provides examples for CI dependency scans and threshold checks.
Guides SBOM, SARIF, and markdown report generation.
Outlines update workflows that include testing and verification.
limitations: Requires dependency manifests or lockfiles to produce useful results.
Depends on locally available scanners and their vulnerability databases.
Automated fixes can change dependency behavior and require approval.
Does not replace runtime security testing or manual threat review.

use_cases.title: Audit a Product Repository
use_cases.description: Review application dependencies, identify high-risk packages, and prepare a prioritized remediation plan.

use_cases.title: Add CI Dependency Gates
use_cases.description: Create scheduled dependency scans and fail builds when critical vulnerabilities are detected.

use_cases.title: Prepare Supply Chain Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate SBOM and vulnerability summaries for compliance reviews and vendor security requests.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Dependency Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository for dependency vulnerabilities. Identify the ecosystems present, summarize critical findings, and recommend next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Vulnerability Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the dependency scan results and create a remediation plan. Group fixes by urgency, owner, testing need, and release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Security Scanning
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI dependency scanning workflow for npm, Python, and Go. Include schedule, failure thresholds, artifacts, and approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Build Supply Chain Reporting
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency security reporting process. Include SBOM generation, SARIF output, executive summary content, and remediation tracking.

output_examples.input: A repository contains package-lock, requirements, and go module files.
output: Ecosystems detected: npm, Python, and Go.
Highest priority: critical and high vulnerabilities with available fixes.
Recommended action: patch direct dependencies first, then retest affected services.

output_examples.input: A team wants recurring dependency checks in CI.
output: Schedule daily scans on the main branch.
Upload scanner reports as build artifacts.
Fail builds when critical vulnerabilities are present.

output_examples.input: A compliance review requests supply chain evidence.
output: Generate an SBOM for each ecosystem.
Attach vulnerability summaries and remediation status.
Record scanner versions and scan dates for traceability.

best_practices: Ask before running commands that install, update, or fix dependencies.
Validate scanner output against project context before changing packages.
Run tests and review lockfile changes after every remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-upgrade major versions without owner approval.
Do not treat scanner severity as the only business priority.
Do not publish SBOMs or reports that expose private package details.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples for npm, Python, Go, and Rust dependency scanning.

faq.question: Can it generate an SBOM?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes CycloneDX-style SBOM guidance and reporting patterns.

faq.question: Does it run scanners automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Commands should run only with user approval.

faq.question: Can it fix vulnerable dependencies?
faq.answer: It can plan fixes and show update workflows, but remediation requires testing and approval.

faq.question: Does it replace a security team review?
faq.answer: No. It supports dependency triage, but humans should review high-risk changes.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
